Feature: Is there an overt marker for the absolutive?
Comment: ABS (intransitive S and transitive O) is zero-marked; no dedicated ABS suffix (§2.3, p.344).
curated_comment: Francisco León Zoque (fran1266, ISO zos, Mixe-Zoque, Mexico) is an ergative language with a person-based split per Engel & Bartholomew (1987). ERG suffix -'is marks transitive subjects and possessors for full NPs and 3rd person demonstratives; 1st and 2nd person grammatical roles are encoded exclusively through verb agreement prefixes. This explains GB409_2=0 and GB409_3=0 while GB409_4=1 and GB409_5=1. All ten '?' values resolved: GB409_6,9,11-13,15-17,21→1 (no conditioning splits found for any of these), GB409_22=0 (no additional conditioning), GB409_23=1 (explicit ERG=GEN syncretism: same -'is marks transitive subjects and possessors). Glottocode fran1266 is correct.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on first person pronouns?
Comment: 1st person pronouns have the same form for subject and object functions (§3.1.4, p.349). Grammatical role of 1st/2nd person encoded through verb prefixes (N-), not through nominal ERG suffix.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on second person pronouns?
Comment: 2nd person pronouns also have invariant form; role encoded through verb prefixes.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on third person pronouns?
Comment: No dedicated 3rd person pronouns; demonstratives serve as 3rd person (§3.1, §3.4) and DO take ERG suffix -'is: je'is (dem-ERG). Confirmed at §3.3 and §2.3.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging on full NPs?
Comment: Full NPs take ERG suffix -'is when transitive subjects (§2.3: 'El viento derribó a un árbol grande' with sava'is = wind-ERG).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the imperfective aspect?
Comment: Continuative/imperfective aspect (-pa) co-occurs with ERG marking: yomo'is tyonvitu'yajpa 'The women turn the tortillas' (§2.1.2). No aspect-based split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the perfective aspect?
Comment: Preterite/completive (-u) also co-occurs with ERG marking (§2.3). No aspect-based split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the past tense?
Comment: Preterite examples consistently show ERG -'is on transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-past tenses?
Comment: Present/continuative and future contexts also show ERG -'is. No tense-based split.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the indicative mood?
Comment: All indicative constructions show ERG marking on 3rd person and full NP transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-indicative moods?
Comment: ERG -'is applies in subordinate and modal contexts (§11.3, §15.2); participial relative clauses explicitly require -'is on transitive subjects (§15.2.1).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the realis status?
Comment: All realis (indicative) contexts show ERG marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the irrealis status?
Comment: Future (manba), conditional (oca si), and purpose clauses (va'co) also show ERG -'is on transitive subjects.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an agentive A?
Comment: ERG marks 'la persona responsable del efecto de la acción del verbo transitivo' (§2.3, p.344).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-agentive A?
Comment: Causative prefix yac- creates transitive constructions with non-volitional/inanimate causers taking ERG -'is (sava'is = wind-ERG, p.344). ERG applies to non-agentive A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a topical A?
Comment: No topicality conditioning described or implied; ERG -'is is a structural case suffix.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of a non-topical A?
Comment: No topicality conditioning; ERG applies equally to non-topical A.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an animate A?
Comment: Animate A consistently takes ERG -'is (all canonical transitive subjects are animate).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in the context of an inanimate A?
Comment: Inanimate causers (e.g., wind-ERG, p.344) also take ERG -'is in causative constructions (§9.2.6).

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in main clauses?
Comment: All primary transitive main clause constructions show ERG marking.

Feature: Is there ergative alignment of flagging in non-main clauses?
Comment: Participial/relative clauses explicitly documented: 'Si el elemento de relativo es el sujeto del verbo transitivo... se une el sufijo ergativo -'is al verbo' (§15.2.1, p.401).

Feature: Is ergative alignment of flagging conditioned by any other factor?
Comment: No additional conditioning beyond the person-based split (1st/2nd: verb agreement only; 3rd/NP: nominal suffix -'is). This split is already captured in GB409_2-3.

Feature: Are the ergative and the genitive expressed by the same marker?
Comment: ERG suffix -'is also marks possessors (§2.2.1, p.342: 'El sustantivo poseedor lleva el sufijo ergativo'). Explicit ERG=GEN syncretism.

Feature: Are the ergative and the instrumental/comitative expressed by the same marker?
Comment: Instrumental/comitative expressed through postpositions (-pit 'with', -ji'n 'with', §5, pp.356-357), entirely distinct from ERG suffix -'is.
